  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "This study reviews the genetic and environmental risk factors for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and how they are modeled in animals and human pluripotent stem cell-derived models, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of each.",
  "what_it_found": "ASD is a complex disorder with significant genetic and environmental influences, and while animal models have contributed to understanding, they have limitations in recapitulating human-specific aspects. Human pluripotent stem cell-derived models are emerging as promising tools for studying ASD.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "While these models have contributed to a wealth of studies that have significantly expanded our understanding of ASD, animal models present with some inherent limitations to translatability, such as their inability to recapitulate human-specific transcriptional paradigms and the protracted development of the human brain [ 25 , 34 , 35 ].",
      "topic": "Animal model limitations"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Over the last decade, human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived 2D models such as induced neurons (iNs) as well as 3D models (organoids, assembloids) have started to bridge this gap [ 36 , 37 ].",
      "topic": "Human stem cell models"
    },
    {
      "quote": "A perfect animal model of ASD is untenable because autism, especially facets of it that arise at the interface of developmental gene expression programs and neuronal circuits, is human specific [ 175 ].",
      "topic": "ASD model challenges"
    },
    {
      "quote": "To this day, a perfect ASD model does not exist.",
      "topic": "Model perfection"
    },
    {
      "quote": "The access to hPSC-derived cell types from a patient’s own cells has been a significant milestone in the development of personalized treatments for NDDs and NPDs.",
      "topic": "hPSC milestone"
    },
    {
      "quote": "While animal models may not model the full spectrum of prenatal, perinatal, or postnatal ASD-related behavior or display species-specific differences in drug sensitivity (for example, the anticonvulsant VPA is required in a much lower dose to induce ASD-related phenotypes in pigs (50 to 75 mg/kg) compared to monkeys [ 149 , 150 ]), ASD remains a primarily behavioral disorder that needs to be modeled in live animals.",
      "topic": "Animal model drug sensitivity"
    }
  ]
}
